Meridian half-zip fleece review

May 2026 · 7 min read

Fleeces are the least glamorous thing in any gear closet, which is exactly why bad ones annoy me so much. The Meridian half-zip costs $58, weighs 11 ounces in a size medium, and has now gone through twelve machine washes, three seasons, one bushwhack, and a week of evenings around a damp campfire without pilling, stretching, or losing its shape. I bought it in April. I am still reaching for it in May. And in October. And in every month between.

The fabric

The body is a mid-weight grid fleece that breathes when you are on the move and blocks just enough wind when you stop. It is not waterproof and does not pretend to be; under a shell it performs as a layer should, and over a base layer it is warm enough to sit around camp in until the frost starts.

The details

The half-zip zips smoothly past the chin without biting it, which is rarer than it should be. The cuffs are snug without being tight. The hem stays put when you reach up. There is no chest pocket, which some people will call a flaw and I call one less thing to lose things in.

After the twelfth wash, the only visible change is that the red has faded to a slightly deeper red. The stitching on the shoulder seam is intact. The zipper pull still catches the garage at the top of its track the way it did on day one — a small manufacturing quirk that I have decided to treat as character.

The verdict

$58 is a fair price for a fleece that does everything asked of it and does not fall apart. For most people that means it is worth the extra money — and for people who have been burned by cheap fleeces before, it is the one worth reaching for.
